sub.limitation: minor: belonging or fear of being left out not offered as alternative motive.

sub.limitation: minor: fear of isolation as friends pair off left unexamined.

sub.limitation: minor: unknowns not ranked by consequence.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: 11 turns, all 37-46 words, digestible throughout.

sub.example: Few recaps; each turn adds a step.

sub.example: T7 fertility window raises real stakes from the issue itself.
sub.limitation: minor: tension stays polite and low throughout.

sub.limitation: minor: Dissenter's two concessions (T5, T8) follow a scripted pattern.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: T2 Thoreau's drummer gives the Dissenter some colour.
sub.limitation: minor: voices restrained; Thoreau lacks his sardonic bite.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: T1 'a ruler you never chose'; T9 'alarm with no label'.
sub.limitation: minor: few concrete images beyond T6's ordinary Tuesday.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: T7-T8 brief rise in stakes.
sub.limitation: material: near-identical turn lengths and even tone give flat rhythm.

strengths: T7 social-versus-practical clocks distinction drives T8 reversal and T9 'what would you be late for'.
T3-T4 separate uncertainty from refusal and wanting from relief, giving real reflection material.
Section E converts the debate into observable conditions and small reversible trials.
weaknesses: Nobody raises friendship drift or belonging as what 'behind' may mean.
Values never elicited: T10 says build your own ruler but asks nothing about the user's.
Flat rhythm: identical-length polite turns; Experimenter never answers T4's contamination objection.
editorNotes: Require one turn to name a consideration none of the minds' books covers, such as social or relational loss.
Require a mind to ask the user a direct values question with what each answer would imply.
Require the targeted mind to answer each named objection in its next turn before moving on.
Vary turn length and intensity deliberately; allow one short, sharp turn.
